fix.summary: Fixed all four open findings for the step-3 records unit in /Users/jmagady/dev2/vsdd-factory. (1) S3R-records-C2-1 (major): commits.py's flush now runs its commit-listing diff with --no-renames so a renamed state file commits as both its deletion and its addition; staging splits paths still in the worktree (git add -A) from paths gone from it (git rm --cached -q --ignore-unmatch), so a deletion already staged by a killed flush cannot trip add's "pathspec did not match any files"; and the changed set also unions _staged_paths() — the index's own leftovers — because a staged rename is one 'R' status record both prior readers pass over. Audited every other git command in commits.py for rename/deletion/space/non-ASCII/already-staged and added four tests. (2) S3R-records-C2-2 (minor): lock_release now raises StoreBusy (carrying .released) after writing the kept entries whenever a run could not be ended in time, instead of returning silently; cmd_lock catches it and exits 1 naming a kept entry as holder with an error that says a flush is running. Caller-facing change: lock_release can raise StoreBusy, exactly as plan records.md 3 promises — SessionEnd's wait=0.5 call must catch it and read .released. (3) S3B-records-1 (minor): evidence_write stamps a required integer seq under flush.lock (one more than the highest in the subject's directory) and the lookup sorts by (seq, at, file name), so same-second records keep write order; schema, fixtures, and rewrite/spec/records/evidence.md updated. (4) S3B-records-2 (minor): flush's per-kind record checks became commits.record_kinds(), a claim table; a tracked file under the record folders no row claims is refused with a no_validator problem naming the file, state-commits.md says a new tracked record kind must register its validator, and two tests pin it. Every fix was mutation-tested in a scratch copy: reverting each one fails its test. Only files the records unit owns (plus the two named spec files and the outcomes file) were changed. No __pycache__ was left under next/plugins.

All four findings are fixed. I checked each in a scratch copy of next/ (no .venv) by reverting each part of each fix and running the tests:
- S3R-records-C2-1: there are four parts, and each has a test that fails without it. Removing --no-renames from the commit_rels diff fails renamed_story and killed-flush rename. Staging gone paths with add -A fails deletion_already_staged, killed-flush rename and space_and_accents. Dropping the _staged_paths union fails killed-flush rename, and so does _staged_paths without --no-renames. My own probes passed: a rename with spaces and non-ASCII, a staged rename then modified, and a staged rename whose new side was deleted. Each commits and the next flush is clean.
- S3R-records-C2-2: lock_release raises StoreBusy within the wait. Reverting it fails test_lock_release_wait_bounds_the_whole_call and test_cmd_lock_release_while_a_flush_holds_the_lock. Reverting the cmd_lock catch fails the second test.
- S3B-records-1: sorting by (at, name), a constant seq or no seq each fails test_same_second_records_order_by_write; with no seq, 9 evidence tests fail. The schema requires seq (integer, at least 1), the fixtures carry it, and evidence.md states the rule.
- S3B-records-2: disabling the no_validator refusal fails test_flush_refuses_an_unclaimed_record_file. Dropping the closure row fails test_record_kinds_cover_the_shipped_tracked_records. state-commits.md step 3 states the registration rule.

What changed for a caller of lock_release: the signature, the success return (the list of released entries), ValueError with no selector, and the StoreBusy raised when lock.flock is not had within wait (it carries no 'released') are all unchanged. What is new: when an entry's run_end cannot take flush.lock in the budget left, that entry stays in lock.json and its run stays live. lock.json is then written without the entries that were released, and the call raises StoreBusy (code 'busy'). That exception's attribute 'released' lists the entries that were released, which can be empty. Before, the call returned normally in this case. Callers must catch StoreBusy and read busy.released. hook-runner-b's liveness.py reads busy.entries, which is new finding C1-2.

New problems (all minor, filed in rewrite/findings/sources/extra-step3-records-fix-3-confirm.json): C1-1, a validation bypass through glob characters in a file name, which was already there before this round but the C2-1 audit missed it; C1-2, the attribute-name mismatch at the seam; C1-3, cmd_lock calling every StoreBusy 'a flush is running'.

Seen but not this unit's to fix:
- S1's check_paths skips any path outside the artifact areas, so a stray .factory/stray.json commits unchecked. This follows state-core's design.
- Plan records.md D1 says evidence writes never wait on a flush, but evidence_write now waits up to 2.0 s on flush.lock. The spec (records/lock.md, topics/run-lock.md) puts machine-record writes under flush.lock, and in a probe a 321-file flush held the lock for 0.98 s, so I did not file it.

fix.summary: Fixed all three open minor findings from the step3-records second confirmation. (1) flush's path-taking git calls (add -A, rm --cached, commit --only) now run with GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 so record names with glob characters never widen a commit to files flush just rejected, with a new glob-neighbour test and a space-and-accents test turned into a real rename, both verified to fail without the fix. (2) The StoreBusy seam between locks.lock_release and the hook runner's liveness is named and written down: lock_release attaches released (entries let go) and now also kept (entries held back because run_end was busy); liveness._released_under_busy reads 'released'; a new cross-unit test proves a busy second run_end still logs lock.released for the first entry (verified it fails when liveness reads 'entries' again); the misleading docstring sentence is reworded; topics/state-api.md records the contract (the one-clause naming in plan records.md 3 and hook-runner-b.md 4 is the orchestrator's, rewrite/plans/ is not mine to edit). (3) vsdd lock release tells its two StoreBusy causes apart: the busy-run_end case names a kept entry taken from the exception (no longer lock_entries()[0], which could be an unrelated session's entry) with the flush-running error, while a lock.flock timeout says 'the run lock is busy; another release or a survey holds it' with holder null; both cases tested through the command; commands/lock-release.md states both shapes. Outcome file at rewrite/findings/outcomes/step3-records-fix-3-2.json. Files changed: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/{commits,locks,cmd_lock}.py, next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/hooks/liveness.py, next/tests/unit/test_state_{commits,cmds}.py, next/tests/hooks/test_liveness.py, rewrite/spec/topics/{state-commits,state-api}.md, rewrite/spec/commands/lock-release.md. Note: the hook-runner-b builder working in this tree concurrently landed the 'released' rename in liveness.py while this fix ran; I verified the landed seam, aligned its test, and both suites pass together.

Mutation tests, on a scratch copy of next/ without .venv:
- **C1-1 (glob pathspecs):** removing the literal-pathspec env fails `test_flush_does_not_commit_a_rejected_neighbour_of_a_glob_name`. Removing it from just one of add, rm or commit is not caught, but the other calls still keep a.md out of HEAD, so I count C1-1 fixed. The rename test now does a real rename. Its `endswith('nächste Runde.md')` check is weak, because the new name also ends that way, but its HEAD and status checks are real.
- **C1-2 (`released` attribute):** having liveness read `entries` again fails `test_release_logs_a_busy_store` and the new cross-unit test. Removing `busy.released` in locks.py fails the cross-unit test.
- **C1-3 (busy causes):** treating every StoreBusy as a flush fails `test_cmd_lock_release_while_the_run_lock_is_held`. Removing `busy.kept` fails the flush-holds-the-lock test. Putting the holder back to `lock_entries()[0]` passes every test (see still_open).

Not done, and not mine to do: the clause naming StoreBusy.released in rewrite/plans/step-3/records.md section 3 and hook-runner-b.md section 4 was never written. Those plan files are the orchestrator's; the spec (topics/state-api.md) does name it.

What changed for a caller of lock_release:
- The signature, the return value and the exception class are unchanged. It still returns the list of removed entries on success.
- When a matched entry's run_end cannot take flush.lock in time, lock.json is still written with that entry kept and StoreBusy is still raised. That exception carries:
  - `.released`: the entries actually removed and ended. It existed before this round; it is now named as the contract in topics/state-api.md.
  - `.kept`: new in this round. The matched entries held back because their run_end was busy, never empty on that path.
- A StoreBusy from the lock.flock wait itself carries neither attribute; nothing was read or changed.
- The docstring no longer says a caller cannot tell busy from nothing matched.
- hooks/liveness.py now reads `released`.

still_open.problem: The code is fixed but one part of it has no test. cmd_lock._run tells the causes apart by StoreBusy.kept, and the lock.flock timeout says 'the run lock is busy' with holder null; that part has a test that fails without the fix. The run_end case names _names(kept[0]), but the only flush-busy test has one lock entry, so kept[0] and lock_entries()[0] are the same entry. In scratch, putting the holder back to lock_entries(inv.root)[0] leaves test_state_cmds.py passing (6/6). Probe: lock.json holds [sess-other live on repo-a:develop, sess-mine on repo-b:develop], flush.lock is held, and 'lock release' runs with sess-mine's marker. The fixed code names sess-mine; the mutation names sess-other; no test notices.
still_open.proposed_fix: Add a test with two entries: another session's live entry first and the caller's own entry second, flush.lock held by a subprocess, and 'lock release' run with the caller's marker. Assert exit 1, holder.session is the caller's session (the kept entry, not lock_entries()[0]), the error says a flush is running, and lock.json keeps both entries with both runs live.

still_open.problem: New with the C1-1 fix: GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 conflicts with an inherited GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 or GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS=1. git exits 128 with 'global 'literal' pathspec setting is incompatible with all other global pathspec settings'. gitrun.git passes the person's environment through, so for anyone who exports either variable every flush that has changes returns 'failed', hooks included. Probe in scratch: one new decisions/plain.md flushed with either variable set fails on 'git add -A' with exit 128, and so does the next flush. With the env removed (the code before the fix) both commit.
still_open.proposed_fix: Set _LITERAL_PATHSPECS to {"GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS": "1", "GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS": "0", "GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS": "0", "GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS": "0"}; git reads "0" as off. In scratch this made both probes commit and kept test_state_commits.py at 20/20, also with both variables exported for the whole run. Add a test that monkeypatches both variables into os.environ and asserts that flush commits a new packet and that the [ab].md case still keeps a.md out of HEAD.
